title: Chemistry: Atomic structure and periodic table (Test)

questions.q_en: Which of the following philosophers was the first to propose the concept that matter is made of indivisible particles called atoms?
questions.solution_en:
• Democritus was the first philosopher to suggest that matter is composed of tiny, indivisible particles called atoms.

Further Insight:

• Atom is derived from the Greek word "atomos," meaning indivisible.

• Ancient Greek philosophers, such as Democritus, were among the first to propose the concept of atoms.

• He believed that matter is composed of tiny, invisible, and indivisible particles that are in constant motion.

• John Dalton later built on Democritus' idea with his atomic theory.

• Aristotle rejected the atomic theory

• J.J. Thomson discovered the electron.
questions.solution_hi:
• डेमोक्रिटस पहले दार्शनिक थे जिन्होंने सुझाव दिया कि पदार्थ अविभाज्य कणों, जिन्हें परमाणु कहा जाता है, से बना है।

• परमाणु (atom) ग्रीक शब्द "atomos" से आया है, जिसका अर्थ अविभाज्य है।

questions.q_en: Which of the following postulates of Dalton's atomic theory explains the Law of Conservation of Mass?
options_en: Atoms combine in simple whole-number ratios.
Atoms are indivisible in a chemical reaction.
Atoms of different elements have different masses.
Atoms of the same element are identical in mass and properties.
questions.solution_en:
• Dalton's postulate that atoms are indivisible in a chemical reaction directly explains the Law of Conservation of Mass, as atoms cannot be destroyed or created, only rearranged.

• Atoms combine in simple whole-number ratios: It explains the law of definite proportions.

• Atoms of the same element are identical in mass and properties: It shows the consistency within an element..

Further Insight:

• Dalton's Atomic Theory

• Matter consists of small and indivisible particles called atoms.

• Atoms of a given element are identical in mass and properties.

• Atoms combine in simple whole-number ratios to form compounds(law of definite proportions).

• Atoms cannot be created or destroyed in chemical reactions (supporting the Law of Conservation of Mass).
questions.solution_hi: • डाल्टन की यह मान्यता कि रासायनिक अभिक्रिया में परमाणु अविभाज्य हैं, द्रव्यमान संरक्षण के नियम को सीधे समझाती है, क्योंकि परमाणु न तो नष्ट किए जा सकते हैं न बनाए जा सकते हैं, केवल पुनर्व्यवस्थित हो सकते हैं।

questions.q_en: Which subatomic particle was discovered through the cathode ray experiment conducted by J.J. Thomson?
questions.solution_en:
• J.J. Thomson's cathode ray experiment led to the discovery of the electron, a negatively charged particle.

• Proton: Discovered by Rutherford during his gold foil experiment.

• Neutron: Discovered by James Chadwick in 1932.

• Positron: An antimatter counterpart to the electron.

Further Insight:

• Electrons:

○ J.J. Thomson's cathode ray experiment led to the discovery of electrons in 1897.

○ He also proposed the plum pudding model of the atom, where electrons were embedded in a positively charged "pudding."

•
questions.solution_hi:
• जे.जे. थॉमसन के कैथोड किरण प्रयोग से इलेक्ट्रॉन की खोज हुई, एक ऋणावेशित कण।

• प्रोटॉन: रदरफोर्ड ने अपने स्वर्ण पत्र प्रयोग के दौरान खोजा।

• न्यूट्रॉन: जेम्स चैडविक ने 1932 में खोजा।

questions.q_en: According to Rutherford's atomic model, what occupies the majority of the space within an atom?
questions.solution_en:
• Rutherford's gold foil experiment showed that most of the atom is empty space, with a dense nucleus at the center and electrons orbiting around it.

• Neutrons: Located in the nucleus but do not occupy much space.

• Protons: Reside in the nucleus but do not fill the atom's volume.

• Electrons: They orbit the nucleus but still leave much of the atom as empty space.

Further Insight:

• Rutherford's Atomic Model

• Gold Foil Experiment (1909):

• Ernest Rutherford conducted an experiment where alpha particles were directed at a thin sheet of gold foil.

• Most particles passed through, but some were deflected, and a few even bounced back.

• Conclusions from the Experiment:

• Most of the mass and positive charge of the atom is concentrated in a very small, dense region called the nucleus.

• Most of the atom is empty space, allowing the majority of alpha particles to pass through.

• The negatively charged electrons revolve around the nucleus in circular orbits, similar to planets around the sun.

• Limitations:

• Could not explain the stability of the atom, as classical physics predicted electrons would spiral into the nucleus and loose energy while revolving.

•
questions.solution_hi:
• रदरफोर्ड के स्वर्ण पत्र प्रयोग से पता चला कि परमाणु का अधिकांश भाग खाली स्थान है, जिसके केंद्र में एक सघन नाभिक है व उसके चारों ओर इलेक्ट्रॉन परिक्रमा करते हैं।

• न्यूट्रॉन: नाभिक में स्थित परंतु अधिक स्थान नहीं घेरते।

questions.q_en: Which of the following is true according to Bohr's atomic model?
options_en: Electrons revolve around the nucleus in fixed orbits without losing energy.
Electrons can lose energy and spiral into the nucleus.
Electrons have an equal probability of existing anywhere in the atom.
Electrons revolve around the nucleus in elliptical orbits.
questions.solution_en:
• Bohr proposed that electrons move in fixed orbits, and as long as they remain in these orbits, they do not emit energy. Electrons only emit or absorb energy when they jump between orbits.

• Electrons can lose energy and spiral into the nucleus

○ This was a limitation in Rutherford's model, corrected by Bohr.

Further Insight:

• Niels Bohr (1913) improved upon Rutherford's model by introducing quantized electron orbits:

• Electrons move in specific, stable orbits without radiating energy known as Quantized Orbits( discrete orbit).

• When an electron jumps between orbits, energy is absorbed or emitted in the form of light. This explains the line spectra of elements.

• Significance:

• Explained the stability of atoms and the line spectra of hydrogen.

• Limitations:

• Could not explain spectra of more complex atoms.

•
questions.solution_hi: • बोर ने प्रस्तावित किया कि इलेक्ट्रॉन निश्चित कक्षाओं में गति करते हैं, व जब तक वे इन कक्षाओं में रहते हैं, वे ऊर्जा उत्सर्जित नहीं करते। इलेक्ट्रॉन केवल कक्षाओं के बीच कूदने पर ऊर्जा उत्सर्जित या अवशोषित करते हैं।

questions.q_en: Which of the following statements about isotopes is correct?
options_en: Isotopes of an element have different numbers of protons.
Isotopes have the same number of neutrons but different numbers of protons.
Isotopes have the same chemical properties but different physical properties.
Isotopes are different elements with similar atomic numbers.
questions.solution_en:
• Isotopes of an element have the same number of protons (and therefore similar chemical properties) but different numbers of neutrons, giving them different physical properties such as mass.

Further Insight:

TermDefinitionExamples
IsotopesAtoms of the same element with the same atomic number (Z) but different mass numbers (A) due to a different number of neutrons.- Hydrogen Isotopes: Protium (¹H), Deuterium (²H), Tritium (≥H) - Carbon Isotopes: ¹²C, ¹≥C, ¹⁴C
IsobarsAtoms of different elements with the same mass number (A) but different atomic numbers (Z). These have the same total number of protons and neutrons combined.- Argon-40 (⁴⁰Ar) and Calcium-40 (⁴⁰Ca) - Carbon-14 (¹⁴C) and Nitrogen-14 (¹⁴N)
IsotonesAtoms of different elements that have the same number of neutrons but different atomic numbers and mass numbers.- Carbon-14 (¹⁴C) and Nitrogen-15 (¹⁵N) (both have 7 neutrons) - Chlorine-37 (≥⁷Cl) and Potassium-39 (≥⁹K) (both have 20 neutrons)
questions.solution_hi: • किसी तत्व के समस्थानिकों में समान संख्या में प्रोटॉन (व इसलिए समान रासायनिक गुण) होते हैं परंतु न्यूट्रॉनों की संख्या भिन्न होती है, जिससे उनके भौतिक गुण जैसे द्रव्यमान अलग होते हैं।

questions.q_en: Which of the following statements describes a Cation?
options_en: An atom that gains electrons to form a positive charge.
An atom that loses electrons to form a positive charge.
An atom that gains electrons to form a negative charge.
An atom that loses protons to form a positive charge.
questions.solution_en:
• A cation is formed when an atom loses electrons, resulting in a positive charge.

• Gaining electrons forms a negative ion (anion).

• Atoms cannot lose protons without changing their elemental identity.

Further Insight:

•
questions.solution_hi:
• एक धनायन (cation) तब बनता है जब कोई परमाणु इलेक्ट्रॉन खोता है, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप धनात्मक आवेश होता है।

• इलेक्ट्रॉन प्राप्त करने से ऋणायन (anion) बनता है।

• परमाणु अपनी तात्विक पहचान बदले बिना प्रोटॉन नहीं खो सकते।

questions.q_en: Which of the following best describes the Law of Constant Proportions?
options_en: Mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
The relative number and kinds of atoms in a compound are constant.
In a chemical substance, elements are always present in definite proportions by mass.
Atoms combine in simple whole-number ratios to form compounds.
questions.solution_en:
• The Law of Constant Proportions states that in any given chemical compound, the elements are present in definite and constant proportions by mass.

○ Given by Joseph Proust

• Mass can neither be created nor destroyed: Law of Conservation of Mass (by Antoine Lavoisier).

• Atoms combine in whole-number ratios: Law of Multiple Proportions.

Further Insight:

•

•
questions.solution_hi:
• स्थिर अनुपात का नियम कहता है कि किसी भी दिए गए रासायनिक यौगिक में, तत्व द्रव्यमान के अनुसार निश्चित व स्थिर अनुपात में मौजूद होते हैं।

○ जोसेफ प्राउस्ट द्वारा दिया गया

• द्रव्यमान न तो बनाया जा सकता है न नष्ट: द्रव्यमान संरक्षण का नियम।

questions.q_en: Which of the following correctly defines the atomic number (Z) of an element?
options_en: The number of neutrons in an atom's nucleus.
The sum of protons and neutrons in an atom's nucleus.
The number of protons in an atom's nucleus.
The number of electrons in the outermost shell.
questions.solution_en:
• The atomic number (Z) of an element is the number of protons present in its nucleus.

○ It is this number that defines the element.

○ For example, the atomic number of Hydrogen is 1, meaning it has 1 proton.

• The sum of protons and neutrons gives the mass number, not the atomic number

• The number of electrons in the outermost shell defines the element's valency.

Further Insight:

•
questions.solution_hi:
• किसी तत्व की परमाणु संख्या (Z) उसके नाभिक में मौजूद प्रोटॉनों की संख्या है।

○ यही वह संख्या है जो तत्व को परिभाषित करती है।

○ उदाहरण के लिए, हाइड्रोजन की परमाणु संख्या 1 है, अर्थात इसमें 1 प्रोटॉन है।

questions.q_en: Who is credited with publishing the first modern periodic table and predicting the existence of unknown elements?
questions.solution_en:
• Dmitri Mendeleev is considered the father of the modern periodic table.

• Henry Moseley introduced the concept of atomic number but did not develop the first periodic table.

Further Insight:

• Dmitri Mendeleev is considered the father of the modern periodic table.

○ In 1871, he arranged elements based on atomic mass

○ He left gaps for undiscovered elements, predicting their properties with remarkable accuracy.such as

■ Eka-Boron: later found and named as Scandium

■ Eka-Aluminum: later named as gallium

■ Eka-Silicon: later named as germanium

○ Limitation of Mendeleev Periodic Table

■ He can't explain the position of Hydrogen, which show properties of Halogen but placed in Alkali Metals

■ Not able to explain isotopes.

■ Elements with different properties grouped together.

•
questions.solution_hi:
• दिमित्री मेंडेलीव को आधुनिक आवर्त सारणी का जनक माना जाता है।

• हेनरी मोसले ने परमाणु संख्या की अवधारणा पेश की परंतु पहली आवर्त सारणी विकसित नहीं की।

questions.q_en: What happens to the atomic radius as you move down a group in the periodic table?
options_en: It first increases and then decreases
questions.solution_en:
• As we move down a group in the periodic table:

○ The atomic radius increases due to the addition of electron shells.

○ Each added shell places the outermost electrons farther from the nucleus, increasing the overall size of the atom.

Further Insight:

•
questions.solution_hi:
• जैसे-जैसे हम आवर्त सारणी में किसी समूह में नीचे जाते हैं:

○ इलेक्ट्रॉन कोशों के जुड़ने के कारण परमाणु त्रिज्या बढ़ती है।

○ प्रत्येक जोड़ा गया कोश सबसे बाहरी इलेक्ट्रॉनों को नाभिक से दूर रखता है, परमाणु का समग्र आकार बढ़ाते हुए।

questions.q_en: Which of the following properties generally increases as you move from left to right across a period in Periodic Table?
questions.solution_en:
• As we move from left to right across a period, the ionization energy increases.

○ This is because the nuclear charge becomes stronger, making it harder to remove an electron from the outer shell.

• Atomic size decreases across a period due to stronger nuclear forces pulling electrons closer.

• Metallic character decreases as you move across a period, with non-metals becoming more prominent.

• The number of electron shells remains constant across a period; it only increases down a group.

Further Insight:
questions.solution_hi:
• जैसे-जैसे हम किसी आवर्त में बाएँ से दाएँ जाते हैं, आयनन ऊर्जा बढ़ती है।

○ ऐसा इसलिए है क्योंकि नाभिकीय आवेश मजबूत होता जाता है, जिससे बाहरी कोश से इलेक्ट्रॉन निकालना कठिन होता जाता है।

• परमाणु आकार आवर्त में घटता है।

questions.q_en: The elements from which block in the periodic table are known as the transition metals?
questions.solution_en:
• d-block elements are known as transition metals.

○ These elements occupy Groups 3 to 12 in the periodic table and exhibit properties like variable oxidation states and the ability to form colored compounds.

Further Insight:

• The Periodic Table is also divided into four blocks based on the electron configuration of elements:

○ s-block: Includes alkali metals (Group 1) and alkaline earth metals (Group 2). Examples: Sodium (Na), Calcium (Ca).

○ p-block: Consists of Groups 13 to 18, including metalloids and nonmetals. Examples: Oxygen (O), Chlorine (Cl), Neon (Ne).

○ d-block: Comprises transition metals (Groups 3 to 12). Examples: Iron (Fe), Copper (Cu). These metals often form colored compounds and exhibit variable oxidation states.

○ f-block: Contains lanthanides (atomic numbers 58-71) and actinides (atomic numbers 90-103). All actinides are radioactive. Example: Uranium (U)

•
questions.solution_hi:
• d-ब्लॉक तत्वों को संक्रमण धातु कहा जाता है।

○ ये तत्व आवर्त सारणी में समूह 3 से 12 में स्थित हैं व परिवर्तनशील ऑक्सीकरण अवस्थाओं व रंगीन यौगिक बनाने की क्षमता जैसे गुण प्रदर्शित करते हैं।

questions.q_en: Which of the following statements about nonmetals is correct?
options_en: They are good conductors of electricity.
They form covalent bonds with other elements.
They generally have high melting and boiling points.
questions.solution_en:
• Nonmetals tend to form covalent bonds with other elements.

• They share electrons in their outer shell to achieve stability, as seen in compounds like H2O (water) and CO2 (carbon dioxide).

• Nonmetals are poor conductors of electricity, unlike metals.

• Nonmetals are generally brittle, not malleable or ductile.

• Nonmetals typically have low melting and boiling points, except for a few like carbon (diamond).

Further Insight:

• Based on their physical and chemical properties, elements are categorized as:

○ Metals:

■ Good conductors of heat and electricity.

■ Form ionic compounds and alloys.

■ Examples: Iron (Fe), Gold (Au).

○ Non-metals:

■ Typically form covalent bonds.

■ Can exist as solids, liquids, or gases.

■ Examples: Oxygen (O), Nitrogen (N).

○ Metalloids:

■ Exhibit properties of both metals and non-metals.

■ Examples: Silicon (Si), Arsenic (As).
questions.solution_hi:
• अधातुएँ अन्य तत्वों के साथ सहसंयोजक बंध बनाने की प्रवृत्ति रखती हैं।

• ये स्थिरता प्राप्त करने हेतु अपने बाहरी कोश में इलेक्ट्रॉन साझा करती हैं, जैसा H2O (पानी) व CO2 (कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड) जैसे यौगिकों में देखा जाता है।

• अधातुएँ विद्युत की कुचालक होती हैं।

questions.q_en: Which of the following is a key difference between Mendeleev's periodic table and the modern periodic table?
options_en: Mendeleev's table was based on atomic number.
Mendeleev's table grouped elements based on their properties.
Modern periodic table arranges elements by atomic number.
Modern periodic table does not include any gaps for undiscovered elements.
questions.solution_en:
• The modern periodic table is based on the atomic number, whereas Mendeleev's table was based on atomic mass.

• The modern periodic law states that properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic number.

Further Insight:

• Dmitri Mendeleev is considered the father of the modern periodic table.

○ In 1871, he arranged elements based on atomic mass

○ He left gaps for undiscovered elements, predicting their properties with remarkable accuracy.such as

■ Eka-Boron: later found and named as Scandium

■ Eka-Aluminum: later named as gallium

■ Eka-Silicon: later named as germanium

○ Limitation of Mendeleev Periodic Table

■ He can't explain the position of Hydrogen, which show properties of Halogen but placed in Alkali Metals

■ Not able to explain isotopes.

■ Elements with different properties grouped together.

•
questions.solution_hi:
• आधुनिक आवर्त सारणी परमाणु संख्या पर आधारित है, जबकि मेंडेलीव की सारणी परमाणु द्रव्यमान पर आधारित थी।

• आधुनिक आवर्त नियम कहता है कि तत्वों के गुण उनकी परमाणु संख्या के आवर्ती फलन हैं।

questions.q_en:
Consider the following statements regarding trends in the periodic table:

a. Atomic radius increases across a period from left to right.

b. Electronegativity increases as you move from left to right in a period.

c. Ionization energy decreases down a group.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution_en:
• Atomic radius decreases across a period due to increasing nuclear charge.

• Electronegativity increases across a period as elements become more eager to attract electrons.

• Ionization energy decreases down a group because the outermost electrons are farther from the nucleus and easier to remove.

Further Insight:

• Trends in the Periodic Table

• Atomic Radius:

○ Increases down a group due to the addition of electron shells.

○ Decreases across a period as the nuclear charge pulls electrons closer.

• Ionization Energy:

○ Decreases down a group (electrons are further from the nucleus).

○ Increases across a period (more energy needed to remove electrons).

• Electronegativity:

○ Decreases down a group.

○ Increases across a period, with Fluorine (F) being the most electronegative element.

• Electron Affinity:

○ Increases across a period (except noble gases).

○ Decreases down a group.

•
questions.solution_hi:
• बढ़ते नाभिकीय आवेश के कारण आवर्त में परमाणु त्रिज्या घटती है।

• इलेक्ट्रॉन ऋणात्मकता आवर्त में बढ़ती है क्योंकि तत्व इलेक्ट्रॉनों को आकर्षित करने हेतु अधिक उत्सुक हो जाते हैं।

• आयनन ऊर्जा किसी समूह में नीचे जाने पर घटती है।

questions.q_en:
Consider the following statements regarding the p-block elements:

a. The p-block contains both metals and nonmetals.

b. The elements in Group 17 are called transition elements.

c. The noble gases are part of the p-block.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution_en:
• The p-block contains a variety of elements, including metals, nonmetals, and metalloids.

• Group 17 elements are halogens, not transition elements.

• Noble gases (Group 18) belong to the p-block.

Further Insight:

• p-Block Elements:

• Contains metals, metalloids, and nonmetals.

• Includes noble gases (Group 18).

• Groups: 13 to 18

• Group 13: Boron (B), Aluminium (Al), Gallium (Ga), Indium (In), Thallium (Tl).

• Group 14: Carbon (C), Silicon (Si), Germanium (Ge), Tin (Sn), Lead (Pb).

• Group 15: Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), Arsenic (As), Antimony (Sb), Bismuth (Bi).

• Group 16: Oxygen (O), Sulfur (S), Selenium (Se), Tellurium (Te), Polonium (Po).

• Group 17 (Halogens): Fluorine (F), Chlorine (Cl), Bromine (Br), Iodine (I), Astatine (At).

• Group 18 (Noble Gases): Helium (He), Neon (Ne), Argon (Ar), Krypton (Kr), Xenon (Xe), Radon (Rn).
questions.solution_hi:
• p-ब्लॉक में धातु, अधातु व उपधातु सहित विभिन्न प्रकार के तत्व शामिल हैं।

• समूह 17 के तत्व हैलोजन हैं, संक्रमण तत्व नहीं।

• उत्कृष्ट गैसें (समूह 18) p-ब्लॉक से संबंधित हैं।

questions.q_en:
Consider the following statements about the f-block elements:

a. Lanthanides are part of the f-block and exhibit similar chemical properties.

b. Actinides in the f-block are mostly non-radioactive.

c. The f-block elements are also known as inner transition metals.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution_en:
• Lanthanides exhibit similar properties due to the filling of 4f orbitals.

• Actinides are mostly radioactive, with some being highly unstable.

• f-block elements are referred to as inner transition metals due to their position in the periodic table.

Further Insight:

• f-Block Elements (Inner Transition Metals):

• Lanthanoids (Atomic numbers 57 to 71):

• Silvery-white metals, high melting points.

• Common oxidation state: +3.

• Examples: Lanthanum (La), Cerium (Ce), Neodymium (Nd), Europium (Eu), etc.

• Actinoids (Atomic numbers 89 to 103):

• All are radioactive.

• Examples: Thorium (Th), Uranium (U), Plutonium (Pu), etc.

questions.q_en:
Consider the following statements about the s-block elements:

a. The s-block contains alkali metals and alkaline earth metals.

b. Elements of the s-block generally form covalent compounds.

c. All s-block elements are metals.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution_en:
• The s-block consists of Groups 1 and 2, which include alkali metals and alkaline earth metals.

• s-block elements typically form ionic compounds.

• All elements in the s-block are metals, such as sodium and calcium.

Further Insight:

• s-Block Elements:

• Groups: 1 (Alkali metals) and 2 (Alkaline earth metals).

• Group 1: Lithium (Li), Sodium (Na), Potassium (K), Rubidium (Rb), Cesium (Cs), Francium (Fr).

• Group 2: Beryllium (Be), Magnesium (Mg), Calcium (Ca), Strontium (Sr), Barium (Ba), Radium (Ra).

• Properties:

• Highly reactive metals.

• Form ionic compounds.

• Low ionization energy and electropositivity.
